chapter: Clarinet fingering and the Tio family
title: Tio's patched-up clarinet and the trip to New York
summary: His wife is introduced; Laurent recalls a great clarinetist whose clarinet was held with rubber bands and cork and who was told to buy a new one before a New York trip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: How are you doing? Good afternoon. Yeah, I do.
That's my wife Mr. Russell. Yeah, you do.
Glad to know you. Very nice to meet you.

And he used to play everything for the soul. The only time he got it, they made him get a new clarinet. That's when Peter Arm made his first trip to New York. Peter Arm said, you ought to be shamed. Man, he had rubber bands from top to bottom and cork shoving them holes from top to bottom. You know, I said, you can't go to New York with that. Not a great musician like you. He says, oh, you ought to be shaming. So he bought a new one. But he didn't want no new one. He wanted that old one. Used to the thing. Oh man, he could play that old thing. You swear I said it was a $50,000 clarinet he was playing.
Do you remember what make it was, Albert? Do you remember the make of it? Whether it was a... Excuse me?

Oh no, I don't remember the make exactly. But it was Albert system. It was Albert system. I don't know if it was a pencil, or a pencil, or a pencil. But he had Albert system like me. He had loved Albert system. The same number of keys on it and everything like that? Fifteen keys, yeah. Our system.
When you say he stopped up the holes, would that be where the keys were, or where the finger holes? Where the key was anywhere.
Anyplace it would break. Anywhere it would break.

He said, I don't need that no more. Oh man, he was great. He was great on catching them keys that could close up them holes and don't think nothing about it. Hit them notes below, above the staff, above the staff hole. He'd make that same note. That note, the ear in the staff yell would be broke. He'd make ear below the staff, over the first line, above the staff. Oh yeah.
